list: Official PlayStation 5 trophy list (55 trophies) as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide text written for this entry and cross-checked against the published guides named in each trophy's sources.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum itself: it pops on its own once the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing separate to chase. Use this tracker as your checklist and treat every other entry here as one line of this trophy. PowerPyx and PSNProfiles both frame the platinum as a completion award rather than a task, which matches the official description.
steps: Earn the other 54 trophies.
Let the platinum pop automatically — no extra action is needed.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks at the very end, the moment the 54th other trophy is earned.
trophies.pitfalls: Do not leave a cumulative counter (choices, stunts, spending) to the last minute; those are the trophies that actually delay this one.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: A story award for finishing Gone Fishing, the mission named in the official description. Simply play it through to its end; KeenGamer and Push Square both treat it as unmissable story progression, so no preparation or choice is required.
steps: Play Gone Fishing to completion.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when Gone Fishing is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: None known — it cannot be skipped if you play the story. Skipping cutscenes does not affect it.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every main mission of Chapter 1 and the trophy lands as the chapter closes. Before you cross that point, clear the Chapter 1 meditation spot for Positive Mental Attitude (see its entry) — PowerPyx-style roadmaps put that errand inside this chapter for a reason, in case its window may close with the chapter.
steps: Work through the Chapter 1 story missions in order.
Before finishing the chapter, complete the Chapter 1 meditation spot.
Complete the final Chapter 1 mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks at the end of Chapter 1.
trophies.pitfalls: Ending Chapter 1 may close the window for the Chapter 1 meditation spot tied to Positive Mental Attitude — the one potential missable in the list.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Play Chapter 2's main missions through to the chapter finale. It is a pure story-progression award (the name is shown exactly as PlayStation publishes it, asterisks included), and the guides checked list no side condition for it.
steps: Continue the main story into Chapter 2.
Complete the chapter's final mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks at the end of Chapter 2.
trophies.pitfalls: None — story progression only. Keep chipping at cumulative counters between missions so they never become an endgame wall.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete the main missions of Chapter 3. Like the other chapter trophies this one is awarded for story progression alone; GTA-Zone and KeenGamer chapter summaries agree there is no optional condition attached.
steps: Continue the main story into Chapter 3.
Complete the chapter's final mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks at the end of Chapter 3.
trophies.pitfalls: None — story progression only.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4's main missions. By this point most activity and collectible systems are open, so Push Square's approach — alternate story missions with map cleanup — keeps the endgame short without risking this purely story-based award.
steps: Continue the main story into Chapter 4.
Complete the chapter's final mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks at the end of Chapter 4.
trophies.pitfalls: None — story progression only.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The gold story award: finish the game's final mission. Whatever choices the finale offers, the trophy is for completing it; keep a manual save before the endgame if you want a clean return point for cleanup.
steps: Reach the final mission through the main story.
Complete it, whichever way the finale plays out.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks at the end of the main story.
trophies.pitfalls: Make a backup save before the finale for cleanup.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the named story mission Breakfast Run. It sits on the main path, so following the story markers earns it.
steps: Follow the main story until Breakfast Run is offered.
Complete the mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the story mission Breakfast Run is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: None known — a main-path mission cannot be permanently skipped.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist, a named set-piece mission on the main story path. Prepare as you would for any heist-style mission — arrive stocked and follow the mission objectives — but the award itself only asks for completion, per the official description.
steps: Progress the story until The Cartel Heist begins.
Complete the heist mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when The Cartel Heist is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: None known for the trophy itself; failing a mission section just means retrying that section.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. It is tied to a named mission rather than a chapter, so watch the mission list as you advance the story; completion is the only condition the official list states.
steps: Progress the story until Child's Play is available.
Complete the mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the mission Child's Play is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: None known — main-path story content.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. As with the other named-mission trophies, the official description asks only for completion, and the guides that list it place it on the main path rather than among optional content.
steps: Progress the story until Headliners is available.
Complete the mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the mission Headliners is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: None known — main-path story content.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete VCIA Takedown, the named VCIA mission set the list also references in Catch Me If You Can. Completion is the whole requirement; play it as part of normal story progression.
steps: Progress the story until VCIA Takedown is available.
Complete the mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the mission VCIA Takedown is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: None known — main-path story content. Do not confuse it with the free-roam VCIA trophy, which is a separate award.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete Operation Savage Glory, another named main-path mission. The official description sets completion as the only bar, and in the guides checked for this entry, no medal, time or no-damage condition is attached to it.
steps: Progress the story until Operation Savage Glory is available.
Complete the mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when Operation Savage Glory is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: None known — main-path story content.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The second gold: raise the in-game completion statistic to 100%. That means working the game's own completion checklist — story, strands, activities, collectibles and exploration — rather than any single task. PowerPyx-style completion guides treat this as the umbrella trophy most others feed into, so track it last and use the in-game percentage to find what is missing.
steps: Open the in-game completion / progress screen and note every unfinished category.
Clear categories alongside their own trophies (story, strands, activities, collectibles, exploration).
Push the statistic to exactly 100%.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks whenever your completion statistic reaches 100%, typically near the very end of a platinum run.
trophies.pitfalls: The last few percent are usually one overlooked category, not a grind — re-read the in-game checklist instead of repeating finished content.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Land 250 stunts in total; PlayStation tracks the count, so the counter on this page mirrors it. Stunts are a repeatable free-roam activity, so the efficient pattern the activity guides describe is to bank them in batches whenever you cross the map instead of saving all 250 for the endgame.
steps: Learn what the game counts as a stunt by completing a few deliberately.
Weave stunt attempts into normal travel across Leonida.
Keep going until the tracked counter reaches 250.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the stunt counter reaches 250, at any point in the game.
trophies.pitfalls: Do not assume a jump counted — check the counter is moving before settling into a long farming session.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every activity type once — the official starter data counts 9 types. This is the sampler trophy: each type only needs a single attempt, so sweep them early to learn which activities you enjoy before their dedicated trophies ask for wins and gold medals.
steps: Open the map / activity list and note each distinct activity type.
Play one session of each of the 9 types.
Confirm the tracked count reaches 9.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks once all 9 activity types have been tried at least once.
trophies.pitfalls: Trying the same activity at a second location is not a new type — variety, not volume, is what counts.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold-medal every Shooting Range challenge — 42 of them, and PlayStation tracks the gold count. Work range by range, learn each challenge's scoring, and replay immediately while the layout is fresh; Push Square and PowerPyx both treat range golds as a practice trophy, not a luck trophy, so short focused retries beat marathon sessions.
steps: Find a Shooting Range and clear its challenges at any medal level first.
Replay each challenge until it scores gold.
Repeat at every range until the counter shows 42 golds.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the 42nd Shooting Range challenge is gold-medalled.
trophies.pitfalls: Leaving one stubborn challenge to the end is fine, but log which one it is in the notes field here so it is not forgotten.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win the Top Fun drone race at each of its 14 locations — a win per location, not just an entry. Learn a course with a practice run, then race it clean; the race guides' consistent advice is that a tidy line beats raw speed on unfamiliar courses.
steps: Enter the Top Fun race at a location and learn the course.
Win it, then move to the next location.
Repeat until all 14 locations show a win.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the 14th location's drone race is won.
trophies.pitfalls: Entering is not winning — only first place advances this counter.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different is the operative word, so one favourite race won 20 times does not finish this. Keep a tally of which races you have already won (the notes field here works well) and rotate through the race list.
steps: Pick an unwon race from the race list.
Win it and record it.
Repeat with new races until the counter reaches 20.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks at your 20th distinct race win.
trophies.pitfalls: Re-winning the same race does not advance the count — track the distinct ones.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Out-fish Cal in a head-to-head fishing challenge. The trophy asks for one win against this named rival, so learn the fishing loop first in free play, then take the challenge when the mechanics feel routine, as the activity guides suggest for rival challenges generally.
steps: Practise fishing until casting and reeling feel comfortable.
Accept Cal's fishing challenge.
Score better than Cal to win it.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks the first time you beat Cal in his fishing challenge.
trophies.pitfalls: Going in cold wastes the attempt's learning value — practise first, challenge second.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Finish one arcade game, start to finish. Any cabinet counts as long as the game is completed rather than merely played, so pick the shortest or most familiar title you find and see it through to its end screen.
steps: Find an arcade cabinet and start a game.
Play it through to completion.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when an arcade game is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: Quitting mid-game does not count — the description says complete, not play.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's strand by completing his final mission. Strand trophies like this one ask for the whole chain, so work Andy's missions whenever they appear on the map and the finale will offer itself; PSNProfiles-style strand lists group these by giver, which is how the roadmap stage here is organised too.
steps: Start Andy's mission strand when it appears.
Complete each of his missions in order.
Finish his final mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when Andy's final mission is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: A strand only advances when its current mission is done — if the finale never appears, an earlier Andy mission is still outstanding.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's final mission to close his strand. Keep his chain moving alongside the story so the finale is available well before your endgame cleanup, and use the in-game strand tracking to confirm which step you are on.
steps: Start Kenton's strand when it appears.
Work through his missions in order.
Complete his final mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when Kenton's final mission is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: Strand finales can hide behind an unfinished mid-strand mission — check the chain before assuming a bug.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's strand with his final mission. As with the other named-giver trophies, completion of the whole chain is the requirement and the official description names only the finale, so steady progress through his missions is the entire method.
steps: Start Billy's strand when it appears.
Complete his missions in order.
Finish his final mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when Billy's final mission is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: None beyond keeping the strand moving — a stalled chain means a mission is waiting somewhere.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida; PlayStation tracks the strand count. The individual giver trophies (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and others) each feed this total, so finishing strands you have already started is the fastest route to 8.
steps: Finish strands already in progress — each completed strand counts once.
Start new stranger strands until the counter reaches 8.
Confirm the silver pops at the eighth completed strand.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the 8th stranger strand is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: A started strand is not a completed one — only finished chains advance the counter.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission to close his strand. Work his missions as they surface and this lands naturally inside the Stage 3 strand sweep; no extra condition is stated in the official description.
steps: Start Randy's strand when it appears.
Complete his missions in order.
Finish his final mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when Randy's final mission is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: Keep the chain moving — the finale only appears after the earlier steps are done.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's strand by completing his final mission. The method is the same steady chain-clearing as the other giver trophies; batching all strands into one roadmap stage keeps their locations and givers from blurring together.
steps: Start Tyrone's strand when it appears.
Complete his missions in order.
Finish his final mission.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when Tyrone's final mission is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: None beyond finishing the whole chain.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Potential missable — handle with care. Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida; one of them is a balcony meditation tied to Chapter 1, and the safe reading of the published guides is that its window closes when Chapter 1 ends. The sources do not fully pin down that spot's exact position, so the safe default is simple: meditate at the Chapter 1 balcony spot during Chapter 1, before you finish the chapter, then collect the remaining spots at leisure — they stay available in free roam.
steps: During Chapter 1, find and use the balcony meditation spot before completing the chapter.
After the story, meditate at each remaining spot across Leonida.
Check the counter reaches 18.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the 18th meditation spot is used. The Chapter 1 balcony spot is the risk: bank it during Chapter 1, before the chapter ends, in case the window reading is right.
trophies.pitfalls: POTENTIAL MISSABLE: finishing Chapter 1 without the balcony meditation may lock that spot for the rest of the playthrough. Do it first; do not trust cleanup to save you.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Track and hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. This is a one-off contract rather than a repeatable hunt, so follow Bret's strand until the hunt is offered, then complete it as directed in-game; the official description names the giver and the quarry type and nothing more specific is confirmed.
steps: Progress Bret's requests until the unique-animal hunt is offered.
Track the animal using the in-game prompts.
Complete the hunt for Bret.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the unique animal has been hunted for Bret.
trophies.pitfalls: Do not expect random wildlife encounters to substitute — it is one specific hunt tied to Bret.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full collectible card sets. Cards are found set by set, so focus on finishing one set at a time instead of scattering pickups; the collectible guides' standard advice — sweep an area fully before moving on — applies directly, and the notes field here is a good place to log partial sets.
steps: Pick one card set and collect every card in it.
Repeat for a second set.
Finish a third set to reach the tracked target of 3.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the third card set is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: Loose cards from many sets finish nothing — completed sets are what the counter tracks.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It action at 100 different locations, with PlayStation tracking the total. Treat it as a background collectible: whenever you arrive somewhere new, do it once before moving on, and the 100 accumulate across normal play instead of becoming one long endgame lap.
steps: Use WAiNK It whenever you reach a new location.
Vary your route so locations do not repeat.
Continue until the counter reaches 100.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks at the 100th distinct location.
trophies.pitfalls: Repeating it in the same spot does not help — the description counts locations, so keep moving.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges of any kind. The counter tracks game-wide challenge completions, so it fills naturally while you work through activities and other challenge content, and any shortfall is a quick cleanup at the end.
steps: Complete challenges as part of the activity sweep.
Check the counter in the tracker as you go.
Top up with any remaining challenge types until it reads 50.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the challenge counter reaches 50.
trophies.pitfalls: Do not grind this separately before the activity sweep — most of it arrives for free.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, raise a 4-star wanted level and then lose it completely. The two conditions are the stars and the company: build the wanted level deliberately in free roam with your partner present, then break line of sight and stay hidden until the heat clears, which is the standard wanted-level routine the free-roam guides describe.
steps: Free-roam with your partner present.
Raise your wanted level to 4 stars.
Evade until the wanted level is fully lost.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks the moment a 4-star wanted level is lost while your partner is with you.
trophies.pitfalls: Losing the stars without your partner present does not count — check they are with you before you start the chase.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Chain three shop robberies with your partner while keeping a wanted level alive the whole time — the run ends if the heat fully drops between shops. Plan a tight route of three nearby shops before starting, rob them in quick succession, and only evade once the third is done.
steps: With your partner, pick three shops close together.
Rob the first and keep the wanted level active.
Rob the second and third back-to-back without losing the heat.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the third consecutive shop is robbed with the wanted level never lost.
trophies.pitfalls: Escaping fully between shops resets the chain — staying wanted is the point of this one.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 distinct vehicles — getting in (or registering) new models as you meet them. Vehicle variety follows area variety, so this pairs naturally with the exploration trophy: tour rich and poor districts, ports and countryside, and hop into anything you have not driven before.
steps: Enter every new vehicle model you encounter.
Tour different districts to widen the pool of models.
Continue until the counter reaches 100.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the 100th distinct vehicle is discovered.
trophies.pitfalls: The same model in a new colour is still the same vehicle — variety of models is what counts.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Down five enemies inside one activation of Combat Focus. Set the moment up before you trigger it: gather a group of five or more hostiles, line yourself up, then activate the ability and work through them quickly, which is how the combat guides frame single-window multi-kill trophies generally.
steps: Find or provoke a group of at least five enemies.
Position yourself with a clear view of the group.
Activate Combat Focus and take down five before it ends.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the fifth enemy falls within a single Combat Focus use.
trophies.pitfalls: Triggering the ability against two or three enemies wastes the setup — wait for a proper crowd.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Leave VCIA in an unscheduled way, in free roam. Head to VCIA outside of missions and get airborne on your own terms; the trophy rewards the improvisation.
steps: Travel to VCIA in free roam.
Get into an aircraft or vehicle and depart on your own terms.
Leave the airport area to make the departure count.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the unscheduled VCIA departure is made.
trophies.pitfalls: VCIA Takedown is a separate mission-completion trophy — this one must be your own doing in free roam.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Unconfirmed trigger — stated honestly: the official description ('Kinda hot in these Rhinos') points at the Rhino tank, but none of the published guides checked for this entry (PowerPyx, KeenGamer, Push Square, GTA-Zone, PSNProfiles, Exophase) confirms the exact action required, whether that is entering, driving, surviving in or destroying a Rhino. Treat any specific method as a guess until a source confirms it; the cautious experiment is to seek out a Rhino in free roam and interact with it, and to re-check the cited guides as their coverage firms up.
steps: Note that the trigger is unconfirmed in the sources checked.
Locate a Rhino tank in free roam when the opportunity arises.
Try interacting with it (entering / driving it) and watch for the pop.
trophies.unlock: Timing unconfirmed — it is tied to Rhinos (tanks) per the official description, but the precise moment is not confirmed by the cited guides.
trophies.pitfalls: Do not trust any guide that states a precise Rhino method as fact — as of this entry's research, the trigger is unconfirmed.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store cleanly, with no detection at any point. Scout the store first, plan your entry and exit, and move quietly; if you are spotted, leave and reset rather than finishing a blown attempt, since the description makes no-detection a hard condition.
steps: Choose a jewelry store and observe it before entering.
Enter and rob it without raising detection.
Get out clean to bank the trophy.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when a jewelry store robbery is completed undetected.
trophies.pitfalls: Detection at any moment voids the attempt — a loud finish does not count even if the robbery succeeds.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape after each — the escape is part of the requirement, so a vault emptied but a bust on the way out should not be assumed to count. Treat each vault as a small heist: enter prepared, take the vault, and have an exit route in mind before the alarm phase begins.
steps: Rob a bank vault.
Escape and lose the heat to complete that vault.
Repeat until five vaults are robbed with escapes.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the fifth bank vault robbery ends in a successful escape.
trophies.pitfalls: Getting caught after the vault likely wastes the run — value the escape as much as the robbery.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob one armored truck and get away. Armored trucks are free-roam targets: stop or breach the truck, take what it carries, then lose the response. One clean job is all the description asks for, so pick your moment instead of chasing the first truck you see into a bad position.
steps: Find an armored truck in free roam.
Rob it — breach it and take the money.
Escape and lose the heat.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when an armored truck robbery ends in a successful escape.
trophies.pitfalls: As with the vaults, the escape is written into the description — do not celebrate at the truck.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore the whole state: the tracked total is 52 areas. Exploration registers as you enter new territory, so a deliberate map sweep — district by district, including the outskirts — finishes this faster than hoping story travel covers everything. Pair it with vehicle discovery and WAiNK It stops to make one lap pay three times.
steps: Open the map and identify unexplored areas.
Tour each area until it registers as explored.
Continue until all 52 areas are covered.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the 52nd area of Leonida is explored.
trophies.pitfalls: Fast travel can skip the ground an area needs to register — drive the borders of stubborn areas.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation from each of the 9 gangs — breadth again, not depth: nine different owners, one robbery each. Keep a note of which gangs you have already hit (the notes field here is ideal), because operations do not announce their owners loudly.
steps: Rob an illegal operation and note which gang owned it.
Target operations belonging to gangs you have not hit yet.
Stop when all 9 gangs have been robbed once.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the ninth gang's illegal operation is robbed.
trophies.pitfalls: Robbing the same gang repeatedly adds nothing — variety of owners is the whole requirement.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail at Ocean Beach, somewhere with the view the description mentions. It is a small leisure trophy — the name is shown exactly as PlayStation publishes it, ellipsis included — so do it early while you are learning the map; it sits comfortably inside Stage 1 sightseeing.
steps: Travel to Ocean Beach.
Order or enjoy a cocktail at a spot overlooking the beach.
Let the moment register.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when you enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.pitfalls: None known — a deliberate leisure stop, easy to forget only because nothing forces you there.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive out of a vehicle showroom through its frontage — 'classic style' reads as through the glass, not through the door — the description does not define it further. Take a car inside a showroom and exit by smashing out; that single stunt is the whole trophy.
steps: Enter a vehicle showroom with (or take) a vehicle inside.
Accelerate out through the showroom frontage.
Drive clear.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when you smash out of a vehicle showroom in a vehicle.
trophies.pitfalls: Leaving on foot or through a normal exit does not match the description — the smash is the point.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Bowl at the one named venue: the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley, and follow through — read plainly, complete the bowling activity there rather than just visiting. The name and description are reproduced exactly as PlayStation publishes them, curly apostrophe and all.
steps: Travel to the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
Play the bowling activity there.
Complete it with a proper follow-through.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the bowling activity at that specific alley is completed.
trophies.pitfalls: Bowling anywhere else should not be assumed to count — the description names this alley.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: Unconfirmed trigger — stated honestly: the official description ('A partnership with mass appeal') is deliberately cryptic, and the published guides checked for this entry (PowerPyx, KeenGamer, Push Square, GTA-Zone, PSNProfiles, Exophase) do not confirm what action earns it. It appears to involve the partner characters in some shared feat, but any precise method would be a guess. Leave it for cleanup, watch the cited guides as coverage settles, and do not plan your route around an invented trigger.
steps: Note that the trigger is unconfirmed in the sources checked.
Play partner content naturally as it arises.
Re-check the cited guides for a confirmed method before hunting it deliberately.
trophies.unlock: Timing unconfirmed — the description only establishes a partnership theme.
trophies.pitfalls: Beware confident-sounding methods for this one; none is confirmed by the sources named here.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Screened and cleared — NOT missable. PlayStation tracks this counter to 500 choices, and the count is cumulative across the whole game: every choice the game records, for better or worse, adds to one running total. There is no single decision to get right and no chapter window to miss; just keep playing and making choices, then top the counter up in free play if the story ends short of 500.
steps: Make choices naturally as the game offers them — all of them count toward the one total.
Watch the tracked counter climb toward 500.
If the story ends short, keep making recorded choices in free play until it reaches 500.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the cumulative choice counter reaches 500, whenever that happens.
trophies.pitfalls: Do not restart or reload hunting a 'right' choice for this trophy — the description counts choices made, not choices made well.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Unconfirmed trigger — stated honestly: the description ('Second time's the charm') suggests succeeding at something on a second attempt after a first failure, but the guides checked for this entry (PowerPyx, KeenGamer, Push Square, GTA-Zone, PSNProfiles, Exophase) do not confirm which activity or moment it belongs to. It will very likely pop incidentally during normal play — most players fail and retry something — so do not engineer failures on purpose until a source confirms the specific case.
steps: Note that the trigger is unconfirmed in the sources checked.
Play normally; retries after failures happen on their own.
If it has not popped by cleanup, check the cited guides for a confirmed trigger.
trophies.unlock: Timing unconfirmed — the description implies a success on a second attempt.
trophies.pitfalls: Do not trust a precise claimed trigger for this trophy; none is confirmed by the sources named here.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Unconfirmed trigger — stated honestly: the description ('What the hell just happened?') signals witnessing something strange, in the series' long tradition of odd encounters, but none of the published guides checked for this entry (PowerPyx, KeenGamer, Push Square, GTA-Zone, PSNProfiles, Exophase) confirms a location, event or condition for it. Explore widely — the exploration and strand trophies take you across the whole map anyway — and treat any claimed exact spot as unverified until a cited source backs it.
steps: Note that the trigger is unconfirmed in the sources checked.
Explore the map fully for the other trophies, keeping an eye out for strange events.
Re-check the cited guides as their coverage of this trophy firms up.
trophies.unlock: Timing unconfirmed — it is earned by witnessing something strange, per the official description.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Unconfirmed in detail — stated honestly: the description is vivid ('Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by') and plainly asks you to knock someone down with a melee attack delivered from a moving vehicle, but the guides checked for this entry (PowerPyx, KeenGamer, Push Square, GTA-Zone, PSNProfiles, Exophase) do not confirm the exact setup — which vehicle types qualify, whether the target must be a pedestrian, or how many must fall at once. The description-led attempt is to ride or drive past a target and strike them with a melee drive-by; treat refinements beyond that as unconfirmed.

From a vehicle, pass close by a target on foot.
Strike them with a melee attack as you pass so they are bowled over.
trophies.unlock: Timing unconfirmed beyond the description: it pops when the melee drive-by knockdown is registered.
trophies.pitfalls: Do not assume a specific vehicle or victim count is required — the cited sources do not confirm those details.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder a cumulative $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts — PlayStation tracks the dollar total, so every batch counts and nothing resets. Feed marked bills into the laundering route whenever you hold them instead of stockpiling, and this economy counter fills steadily alongside the robbery trophies that supply the bills.
steps: Acquire Marked Bills through robberies and related free-roam work.
Launder them through your contacts in batches.
Repeat until the tracked total reaches $250,000.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when cumulative laundered Marked Bills reach $250,000.
trophies.pitfalls: Holding bills unlaundered earns nothing here — the laundering, not the stealing, is what the counter tracks.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend a cumulative $100,000 across all shops — every shop purchase counts toward one tracked total. Buy what you actually use (vehicles, gear, services) rather than wasting money on purpose; across a full platinum run, ordinary spending gets most of the way there and a final shopping round closes the gap.
steps: Shop normally throughout the game and let purchases accumulate.
Check the tracked spending total near the end of your run.
Make a final round of useful purchases to pass $100,000 if needed.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when cumulative shop spending reaches $100,000.
trophies.pitfalls: Do not dump cash early on things you will never use — the counter is cumulative, so patience costs nothing.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy every garage property — 8 in total, tracked by PlayStation. Garages are bought with money earned elsewhere, so this is an endgame purchase list: save the locations as they are discovered, then buy the set once your economy trophies have filled the bank.
steps: Note each garage property as you discover it.
Earn enough through robberies, laundering and story play.
Purchase all 8 garages.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the eighth garage property is purchased.
trophies.pitfalls: Spending the money elsewhere first only delays this — ring-fence enough cash once you start the property sweep.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — a small tracked total that pairs perfectly with Whip It Good's 100-vehicle discovery run: whenever you discover a vehicle worth keeping, register it too, and this counter finishes long before the discovery one does.
steps: Discover a vehicle you want to keep.
Register it to the Scooter Bros app.
Repeat until 10 vehicles are registered.
trophies.unlock: Unlocks when the 10th vehicle is registered to the app.
trophies.pitfalls: Discovering is not registering — the app step is separate, so do it on the spot, as the name says.
